s1.syndrome_frame: Acute pruritic skin eruption with vesicles and erythema following sun exposure
salient_findings: Erythema and helical thickening with numerous small blisters on ears
Vesicles at the upper and lower vermillion border
key_facts: 13-year-old boy presented with skin eruption
Eruption appeared 24 hours after intensive sun exposure
Patient reported malaise and headache 2 weeks before presentation
No history of photosensitivity
No use of topical or systemic photosensitizers
Erythema and helical thickening on ears
Numerous small blisters on ears
Vesicles at the upper and lower vermillion border
Erythematous papules and crusts on cheeks, neck, and lower arms
Detectable serum parvovirus B19 IgM and IgG antibodies
PVB19 DNA found in lesional skin biopsy specimen

raw.syndrome_frame: Acute pruritic skin eruption with vesicles and erythema following sun exposure
salient_findings: Erythema and helical thickening with numerous small blisters on ears
Vesicles at the upper and lower vermillion border
key_facts: 13-year-old boy presented with skin eruption
Eruption appeared 24 hours after intensive sun exposure
Patient reported malaise and headache 2 weeks before presentation
No history of photosensitivity
No use of topical or systemic photosensitizers
Erythema and helical thickening on ears
Numerous small blisters on ears
Vesicles at the upper and lower vermillion border
Erythematous papules and crusts on cheeks, neck, and lower arms
Detectable serum parvovirus B19 IgM and IgG antibodies
PVB19 DNA found in lesional skin biopsy specimen

raw.rationale: The presence of detectable serum parvovirus B19 IgM and IgG antibodies and PVB19 DNA in the lesional skin biopsy specimen supports this diagnosis, along with the clinical presentation of an intensely pruritic skin eruption following sun exposure.

rejected.label: Polymorphic light eruption
rejected.why: While this condition is triggered by sun exposure, the presence of PVB19 DNA and antibodies points more specifically to a viral etiology.

rejected.label: Erythema multiforme
rejected.why: This condition typically presents with target lesions and is often associated with herpes simplex virus or other infections, not specifically parvovirus B19.

rejected.label: Hydroa vacciniforme
rejected.why: This rare condition presents with vesicles and scarring after sun exposure, but the presence of PVB19 DNA and antibodies in this case suggests a different etiology.

rejected.label: Solar urticaria
rejected.why: This condition presents with urticarial lesions after sun exposure, but the clinical findings and laboratory results in this case do not support this diagnosis.
